accuracy.evidence: Checked against the Pearson Edexcel A level Mathematics specification (9MA0) Pure 4.2 and 4.4 and the AQA A level Mathematics specification (7357) C4 and C5 on arithmetic sequences and series, nth term and sum to n terms, including proof of the sum formula, and Stewart, Precalculus, on finite arithmetic series. Every lab number was recomputed: pair sums 55, 57, 65; last terms 39, −7, 61; term counts 10, 11, 10; smallest n 15 (S14 = 196, S15 = 225), 18 (S17 = 493, S18 = 549), 9 (S8 = 236, S9 = 252); goals S = 0, 100 and 7 with l = −8.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented series errors: forgetting to halve (prediction 100 versus 50 pairs, challenge 10100 and 310), the nth-term off-by-one a + nd (last-term decoys, prediction 43, challenge 170), counting gaps instead of terms (number line message at n = need − 1, prediction 9, challenge 20), rounding the quadratic root down (smallest-n bars, prediction 14, challenge 12) and keeping a negative root or the later root when d < 0 (falling series round and challenge option ±12.2).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagsum is built on the sum, not the sequence: a reversible copy of the term staircase that only fills every column when flipped and aligned (the reversal proof), partial-sum bars against a target, and a sandbox that shows both sum formulas agreeing. flagarith covers arithmetic sequences as linear functions (slope d, intercept a − d) and flagpasc Pascal's triangle; neither sums terms or uses the pairing argument. The shingle gate passed.

lab_teaches.evidence: Aligning the copy without flipping leaves red overlaps and gaps and column sums 2a, 2(a + d), …; only the reversed copy makes every column a + l, and the caption then reads Sₙ = n × (a + l) ÷ 2. The number line shows n − 1 arcs for n dots, so counting gaps visibly stops one term short. Partial-sum bars make the first crossing, and for d < 0 the rise and fall, visible before the formula is named.

predictions.evidence: Four locked predictions with tempting wrong options: 100 pairs for 1 to 100, 3 + 10×4 = 43 for the 10th term, 9 terms for 5 + … + 50 and 14 for n² ≥ 200. Each following task makes the student act against the wrong option (flip to make 50 pairs visible, pick 39 not 43, slide n to 10, tap bar 15) and the done message quotes the guess.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Five rotating questions with tagged wrong answers, each with its own correction: nohalf (counts both copies), pairs (50 pairs of 101, not 100), nd (adds d ten times), noa (forgets the start), gaps (one more term than gaps), extra (plus one, not two), nd2 (2a + nd), nohalf2 (forgot n/2), down (round the root up) and neg (reject the negative root). Lab taps also name the slip, e.g. 'S14 = 196 is below 200. Rounding the root down lands here.'

readability.evidence: Learner kid text uses short sentences with worked numbers (50 × 101 is 5050) and stays under the learner kid limit of 6.5; the adult text stays under 9.5 while using the exact A level terms arithmetic series, common difference, nth term, sum to n terms, sigma notation, reversal proof, off-by-one and positive integer root.

no_filler.evidence: The filler gate passed. Each kid paragraph carries one step of the argument: Gauss's pairs, the general reversal, the last term, then counting and rounding. Adult paragraphs give the specification statements, the proof, five named mistakes and the lab outline. Overlap with the arithmetic sequences and Pascal's triangle lessons stays under 12 percent.

mobile.evidence: At 390 px the staircase fills 84 percent of the width with bars at least 30 px wide for n = 10, labels at 11 px inside the bars, the number line dots at 8 px radius, partial-sum bars about 15 px wide with labels every 5, and control buttons wrap below the canvas. Long captions use fillText max width so nothing is clipped in light or dark.

accessibility.evidence: walk.cjs: axe found no WCAG 2.1 AA violations in light or dark on desktop and iPhone, no console errors, and every Show me completed. Every canvas action has a button twin (Flip copy, Slide left and right, one button per last-term option, n ± 1 on the line and the bars, a, d and n ± in the sandbox) and the canvas aria-label speaks each result, e.g. 'n = 9 reaches only 45. 9 is the number of gaps (l − a)/d; the terms are one more.'
